processErrors.summary: ChatGPT was instructed to analyze every available Kalshi market for every eligible game before allocating bankroll. It produced a $50 allocation before completing that comprehensive full-market review, and the user placed wagers before ChatGPT later disclosed the review had been incomplete. This is the largest single issue of the night -- a process failure, not merely variance -- and directly explains why Boston F5 (the largest stake, $21.69) went out ahead of Toronto F5 ($14.67), which later had much stronger completed-slate evidence.

Stakes were sized in chronological recommendation order rather than descending validated edge/information quality: Boston F5 ($21.69, incomplete review) outsized Toronto F5 ($14.67, strongest completed-slate edge of the night).

Boston F5 YES and Athletics 4+ runs NO were positively correlated through the same Jake Bennett/Oakland-suppression thesis but were sized as two independent bets ($21.69 + $13.77 = $35.46 combined) rather than one exposure bucket.

Cleveland F5 was a manual override against a negative completed-slate model edge (raw -2.09%, calibrated approx -0.53%). The override reasoning (pitcher-dominance thesis expressed as a team F5 winner) was not captured as a first-class field on the bet at entry time -- a MANUAL_OVERRIDE against a negative model edge should always explicitly document its reason going forward.

A pitcher-dominance thesis (Gavin Williams, 5.2 IP / 2 ER / 7 K) should not automatically be expressed as a team F5 moneyline pick -- it ignores three-way tie risk. Cleveland's F5 lost specifically because the game was 0-0 through five innings, a recurring three-way F5 tie-risk pattern already observed in prior postmortems. Pitcher Ks/outs, opponent team total, F5 total, and NRFI should all be considered as more precise expressions of a pitcher-dominance thesis.

Seattle ML was a late manual re-handicap after Griffin Jax was scratched pregame. The scratch was real, material information, but no fresh standalone price capture / model rerun was performed after it before adding exposure -- Seattle's original standalone snapshot (~52c, confirmed via this import's automatic bet-to-observation linkage: observedPrice=53.0 at 2026-08-08T23:35:25Z) predates the scratch, so it must not be treated as ordinary pre-close CLV against the eventual 54c execution.

Supporting evidence for the existing high-priority engineering fix (build_recommendations.py must map every pipeline market key, especially F5 markets, to the exact archived Kalshi ticker, using explicit not_applicable/not_computed/parser_unresolved states rather than ambiguous nulls): the Aug 8 archived Game dimension table (data/edgelab/games/2026-08-08.jsonl) carries TWO separate gameId rows for CIN@WSH, TOR@PHI, CLE@CWS, and TB@SEA -- one string-form fallback id (scheduledStartTime null) and one numeric mlbGamePk-form id (real scheduledStartTime/mlbGamePk) -- and the corresponding Market dimension table splits that same game's markets across both gameIds inconsistently (e.g. TOR@PHI's F3 markets are indexed under the string-form gameId while its F5/game_result/F7 markets are indexed under the numeric gameId; CIN@WSH's F3/F5/F7/game_result markets are ALL under the numeric gameId only). This is exactly the blocked/missing market identity pattern the engineering fix targets, and it directly caused the bulk importer's automatic away/home game-resolution to pick an inconsistent gameId for 4 of tonight's 6 games (harmless here only because every wager's marketTicker was independently verified and supplied explicitly, bypassing automatic resolution).

proposedInvestigations.summary: Never produce a final bankroll allocation until every eligible archived Kalshi market has been screened for that day's slate.

Tag every recommendation/bet with a provenance field (MODEL_SUPPORTED / MANUAL_OVERRIDE / MODEL_UNAVAILABLE) at entry time, and require a MANUAL_OVERRIDE against a negative model edge to carry an explicit documented reason.
Treat materially correlated bets (same underlying thesis, e.g. Boston F5 + Athletics team-total under) as one exposure bucket for sizing purposes rather than independent stakes.
Explicitly model and communicate tie probability for Kalshi F3/F5 three-way winner contracts before recommending a team-winner pick built on a pitcher-dominance thesis.
Require a fresh standalone price capture / model rerun after a material starter scratch, before recommending new exposure on that game, whenever feasible.
Allocate bankroll in descending order of validated edge/information quality rather than chronological recommendation order.

Continue the existing high-priority engineering fix: build_recommendations.py must map every pipeline market key (especially F5 markets) to the exact archived Kalshi ticker, using explicit not_applicable/not_computed/parser_unresolved field states instead of ambiguous nulls. The Aug 8 slate's dual/fragmented gameId dimension-table rows (see processErrors.MARKET_IDENTITY_FRAGMENTATION) and missing Recommendation ledger for the date (see processErrors.RECOMMENDATION_LEDGER_GAP) are both fresh supporting evidence for this fix.
